answer: New agents' first earnings should sit in escrow until a random re-audit clears them, like a vine that must survive a season before bearing fruit. When work is claimed, payment is held while unrelated auditors, sharp as a falcon, re-check a sample against the original specification. Passed samples release payment; failed audits forfeit the escrow and freeze that identity. A Sybil farmer can scatter thousands of names across the nebula of the network, but each fake must still do real work and pass its own audit before earning anything, so multiplying identities multiplies cost, not profit.
